I want to love this game. On paper, it's everything I want from a game. But to be honest, I still don't get it. I appreciate the effort and the endless updates that have gone into this but there's something about it that just stops it clicking for me. 
I suspect it's the planets themselves. Despite there being lots of different biomes, every planet feels identical. Why does every planet have aliens on them? Why does virtually every planet have cat-bird-dog creatures wandering around? Why does every planet have relics? 
I feel like the entire idea of exploration would be to find these elements out in space and be a reward for exploration, but as far as I can tell, the first planet you get dumped on is fairly representative of the rest of the content.

I bought this game when it originally came out and was so thoroughly disappointed that it was the last preorder I ever made. Now, I wait days after reviews drop to ensure I never run into that issue again.

Everything people were saying about the game back then was completely true. It felt incomplete, grindy as all hell, and you ran out of things to do as soon as you reached the final story mission.

What’s funny is that most of those criticisms are still somewhat true: the game can still feel grindy, the campaign still feels a little incomplete, and the gameplay loop can feel kinda rote by your 40th hour.

What hooks me now, though, is the massive amount of content added through updates and expansions, along with all the custom sliders. You can tune it into a hardcore space sim or turn down the difficulty and resource management to play it as a cozy, low-punishment game.

At the end of the day, I keep coming back for the procedural generation of planets and activities, as well as some of the most beautiful visual sights you can see every time you boot it up.

My opinion of Sean Murray has come full circle—I hate him now for a completely different reason: he won't let me give him more money after a decade of free updates!

Great game, honestly! As someone who knows the struggle of making games like this, and how hard it is to store player data and keep planets looking like planets, I think the devs did a fantastic job. I could never reach this level, even with help. The game they’ve built over 10 years is amazing.

I’m a relatively new player, so I don’t know all the bits and bobs yet, but even when I’m older I bet it’ll still surprise me with new things, animals, and places. It has its glitches here and there, like the odd object floating in the air or clipping into the ground, but nothing major. Honestly, awesome game, and the devs did great to get it where it is today.

The graphics are beautiful too. The colours, the skies, and the planets look stunning, and they still amaze me even though the game is 10 years old. Every time I land on a new planet I stop just to look around.

There’s so much to do as well. You can explore, build bases, trade, fly around in your own ships, and play with friends in multiplayer. It even has VR support, which makes exploring feel even more real. The devs have also kept adding free updates for years, which is rare these days and shows how much they care about the game and the players.

If you check my PC specs, you’ll see basic, bottom-of-the-line parts you probably wouldn’t expect. If your PC is like mine and not too great, GET THE DARN GAME! I get 60 FPS in most scenarios. If you’re worried your PC is “too bad” to run it well, don’t be. The optimization is crazy! Like I said, 60 FPS is pretty good for my PC. Seriously, get the game. It has endless fun and activities, and I’m still not bored. Trust me.

Easy recommend from me!

And there is so much to explore out there! But I’ll let you, whether you’re a newcomer or an old player, figure those things out for yourself. Now go and happy exploring!

I've been playing NMS since launch, and the laundry list of improvements is almost as vast as the universe it's set in.  The game is very enjoyable, but I do have some gripes with it.  

As an example, for all the things I can do in the game, it doesn't really feel like the game is willing to let me pursue any of it, as it's always lighting up my communicator with something else it wants me to check out, "Hey" it whispers, "Go check out that thing" and not even half way through doing so I receive another ping "Hey, there's this other thing that's really cool, go look at that".  Sometimes I just want to shut all quests off and pursue my own thing, but the game doesn't allow for that, and you will forever be interrupted with a to do list that is also nearly as vast as the universe in which the game is set. 

For another the hand holding, annoying as it is, doesn't even do that good of a job explaining what you can and cannot do.  It took far too long for instance, for me to realize that you don't need to do very much gathering of basic resources in the game beyond the first hour or so because you can duplicate most everything else with certain other resources.  Oxygen is a major player in this and is one of the very few resources you need to make sure you have tons of so you can just make the other stuff, but nowhere does the game inform you of this.  And the list is so large you kinda just need to keep the wiki open while playing the game.

These really are just minor gripes though and don't really change my opinion in terms of recommendation.

reviews.review:
First off I have bought this game twice now and have about 200 hours in it. With that experience I can comfortably say the game is fantastically well polished with immense amounts of content. Including story and quest lines, monthly expeditions, system battles, ship and planet hunting, freighter and frigate acquisition, base ship and freighter building, fishing, music making, (Pokémon like) fauna battles, garbage disposal, and much much more.

Some things to note are:
The initial quest lines are a bit extraneous but that is to be expected for being a decade old. Resource gathering, and travel are a major part in this game, and base building can be limiting for knew users, due to the required steps to get all of the currently obtainable components, and limited un-gliched placement options. While the addition of corvettes does certainly help this argument, if you are playing for the building sandbox experience, I would look else ware.

This game is definitely more enjoyable when playing with friends, due to the often repetitive nature, and long story lines if you choose to do them. The first few hours can feel slow, without sufficient amounts of currency or recourses, but it isn't too hard to obtain trillions of units, millions of nanites, and resourced are gathered just by playing, at witch the survival game feels similar to creative mode. 

Additionally Hello Games is now very consistent with there free updates, so it's not unreasonable to say you can expect new content to be dropped every few months. The downside is it can be a lot to pick up as a knew player. Though YouTube guides are abundant, and didn't take me too long to learn about three years back. 

Overall my experience with the game is great, however if you are running a lower end pc such as myself, you can expect a bit of struggle, though nothing that ruins the experience. (It is playable on Nintendo, and now mobile after all). I would personally prefer a bit more freedom when it comes to base building, and customization of such. - But hay that's what Minecraft's for.

If you have yet to give this game a try, I greatly recommend it. 7.8/10
